project.name: Inspection quadcopter
project.summary: An 8 kg-class inspection quadcopter built from real parts: T-MOTOR MN5008 KV170 motors and P18×6.1 propellers on their published bench table, a Tattu 16 Ah 12S pack, a routed ESC with Infineon MOSFETs, TI drivers and an STM32F051 on AM32's pin map, carbon arms checked against blade-pass, and gains flown on real PX4 firmware in simulation. Mass sets thrust, thrust sets current, current heats the MOSFETs, and the sink is mass again. Nothing here has been built: Testing shows what is predicted, what real software has checked, and what has not been run.

headline.label: Thrust to weight, end of charge

optimize.title: Close the weight spiral
optimize.summary: Lightest take-off mass with the ESC MOSFET junction at or below 100 °C and every linked model inside its validated range. Each trial is a full coupled solve.

tour.title: Twelve domains, one solve
tour.text: This project is one file: its design documents, the links between them and this tour. Mass sets thrust through the measured bench table, thrust sets motor current, current heats the MOSFETs, and the sink is mass again. The solver iterates that loop until it settles and says so.

tour.title: Carry a heavier camera
tour.text: A heavier gimbal raises take-off mass. The bench table gives the throttle and current that thrust really takes, and the MOSFET temperature and endurance follow.

tour.title: Grow the ESC heat sink
tour.text: This sink is the lightest the model can vouch for at the real MOSFET currents. Taller fins run cooler, but every motor has to lift them. The Rust electrothermal graph re-solves the sink, and the fluids studio re-solves the duct around it.

tour.title: Save weight on the arms
tour.text: A 30 mm tube is lighter and strong enough, but its first bending mode falls into the rotor's blade-pass band across the flying speed range. Strength alone would have passed it.

tour.title: Slow the gates down
tour.text: A bigger gate resistor slows the MOSFET edges, which rings less but stays longer in the switching region. The loss comes from the datasheet's gate charges at the real phase current.

tour.title: Use thinner copper on the ESC
tour.text: The board is a whole ESC: MOSFETs on Infineon's land pattern, UCC27211 drivers, an STM32F051 wired to AM32's pin map, an LM5017 buck, current and voltage sensing, and poured copper that KiCad's own checks pass. Going to 1 oz copper doubles the resistance the phase current runs through.

tour.title: Turn up the rate gain
tour.text: PX4's own defaults are meant for a much smaller aircraft, so this project carries gains tuned to its inertia and motor lag. Double the rate gain and the model loses phase margin, which is the shape a real over-tuned aircraft shows.

tour.title: Clock the ASIC study faster
tour.text: The flight controller here is a real Pixhawk. This open-source PWM controller and CPU are a study of moving motor control onto a small die, not a part on the aircraft. Its RTL is synthesized onto characterised cells and timed across nine corners; faster clocks cost power and slack.

tour.title: Fly higher for coverage
tour.text: Mission altitude is a Flight output linked into the camera. The Cooke triplet's focal length and the sensor pixel set the ground sample distance.

tour.title: Scoop more rotor wake
tour.text: More of the downwash's dynamic pressure drives the ESC duct. Past Re 2300 the fin channels leave the laminar correlation, and the mechanical model refuses to extrapolate instead of guessing.

tour.title: Charge more packs in the hangar
tour.text: Each charger dissipates the pack energy's 8% loss over a one-hour charge. The charging room uses the BESTEST 600 envelope; its supply air sets its temperature.

tour.title: What has actually been tested
tour.text: Simulations are predictions, and correlation checks a model against measurements it was not fitted to. Real PX4 firmware has flown these gains on a simulated aircraft and KiCad has checked the board, and those results go stale if the design changes. Physical tests stay not run until a person records a measurement. Nothing on this aircraft has been built.

tour.title: Everything above was a command
tour.text: Each step ran through the same registry the command line, scripts, the CLI and the MCP server use. End the tour to restore your design exactly as it was.

plan.title: Thrust to weight at end of charge
ESC efficiency at the design point
Bus ripple at the design point
Thrust model against a motor it was not fitted to
plan.method: T = c·n² fitted to the KV170 bench table, then asked to predict the same propeller on the KV340 motor.

plan.title: Parameters against PX4 v1.17.0's own table
plan.method: Every parameter name, default and range, against the parameters.json PX4 builds. The tuned gains are inside PX4's ranges.

result.note: All 29 parameters exist, every default matches, and the tuned gains are inside PX4's ranges.

plan.title: 15° roll step flown on PX4, against the model
plan.method: Real PX4 v1.17.0 firmware flying this aircraft's mass, inertia, thrust slope and motor lag in its built-in SIH simulator, against this project's own simulation of the same plant.

result.note: Rise 0.275 s on PX4 against 0.275 s in the model; settle 0.920 s against 0.880 s.

plan.title: Rate step overshoot on PX4, against the model
plan.method: 24 steps of 30 °/s averaged by sign, because PX4's simulator injects heavy gyro noise. The result is how far the model's overshoot is from PX4's.

result.note: Overshoot 27.2% on PX4 against 25.6% in the model, 24 steps averaged.

plan.title: Rate-loop crossover on PX4, against the model
plan.method: Identified from a 0.7 to 16 Hz sweep by cross-spectra against the setpoint, which the gyro noise is not correlated with.

result.note: 5.90 Hz on PX4 against 5.65 Hz in the model at the same 250 Hz loop, coherence 0.90.

plan.title: Rate-loop phase margin measured on PX4
plan.method: From the same sweep. Coherence at crossover is above 0.9, so this figure can be trusted.

result.note: The model says 57.1° at the same 250 Hz loop, so it errs on the safe side.

plan.title: Rate-loop gain margin measured on PX4
plan.method: From the same sweep, high in the band where coherence falls away, so this one is weak evidence.

result.note: The model says 7.7 dB. Coherence is 0.24 at 15.0 Hz, so this is weak evidence.

plan.title: KiCad 9.0.9 design-rule errors
plan.method: kicad-cli pcb drc on the exported board after filling zones with KiCad's own filler. The only warnings say the footprint library is not installed.

result.note: 64 warnings, all lib_footprint_issues: the board's footprint library is not installed in KiCad.

plan.title: KiCad unconnected items
plan.method: From the same run. This check found the bus pour cut in two on an earlier layout, which this project's own checks had missed.

plan.title: App Gerbers against KiCad's own copper
plan.method: Overlap of the app's Gerber copper with the copper KiCad computes, per layer, on a 50 µm grid. Pours are pulled back about 0.1 mm by KiCad.

result.note: 99.80% on top, 99.49% on the bottom, on a 50 µm grid.

plan.title: Board against AM32's pin map
plan.method: Every pin AM32 drives on the F0 group B target, read from its source as text, against the net on the STM32F051K8T6 with pin numbers from KiCad's symbol.

result.note: 20 assignments checked. 50.4 V reads 2.80 V at the ADC and 3.15 V at the comparators.

plan.title: AM32 firmware compiled for this board
plan.method: A new target with an 18:1 bus divider, 50 mV/A and 500 ns of dead time, built with arm-none-eabi-gcc. Written but not yet compiled.

plan.title: Weigh the assembled aircraft
plan.method: Ready to fly, with the pack, on a scale good to 10 g. Every estimated mass in Flight gets replaced by a weighed one.

plan.title: Thrust stand on the assembled arm
plan.method: Motor, propeller and ESC on the real arm at hover throttle. Thrust as a percentage of the bench table, which was measured without the arm below it.

plan.title: ESC double-pulse test
plan.method: Peak switch-node voltage at 50 V bus and 15 A, measured with a high-bandwidth probe. The limit keeps 20% below the MOSFET's 100 V rating.

plan.title: ESC thermal soak
plan.method: Hottest MOSFET case temperature after 30 minutes at the design current in the enclosure, with a thermocouple or thermal camera.

plan.title: Arm tap test
plan.method: Accelerometer on the motor mount and an impulse hammer, with the arm clamped in the real centre plates. The model assumes a rigid root, so the real mode is lower.

plan.title: Motor step response
plan.method: Throttle step from hover to 80% on the stand. The rotor time constant from a tachometer or eRPM log replaces the estimate.

plan.title: Tethered hover vibration
plan.method: Peak accelerometer vibration from the flight log, tethered, at hover. Rotor vibration is not in the simulation.

plan.title: Roll step in flight
plan.method: A 15° stick step in the PX4 flight log, with the tuned gains loaded from the parameter file. Compare it with the simulated step.

plan.title: Measured hover endurance
plan.method: Hover in still air until 20% of the pack remains, integrating the power module's current.
